chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Yazīd al-Kunāsī, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), “Was ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (عليه السلام), when he spoke in the cradle, the hujjah of Allah over the people of his time?” He said, “On that day he was a Prophet, the hujjah of Allah, though not sent as a messenger. Do you not hear his statement when he said:”
“Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a Prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me salat and zakat as long as I remain alive.”

I said, “So on that day, in that state while he was in the cradle, was he a hujjah of Allah over Zakariyyā?” He said, “In that state, ʿĪsā was a sign for the people and a mercy from Allah for Maryam when he spoke and spoke on her behalf. He was a Prophet, a hujjah over those who heard his speech in that condition. Then he became silent and did not speak until two years had passed for him, and Zakariyyā was the hujjah of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over the people after the silence of ʿĪsā for those two years.”
Then Zakariyyā died, and his son Yaḥyā inherited from him the Book and the wisdom while he was a small child. Do you not hear the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“O Yaḥyā, hold fast to the Book with strength,” and “We gave him judgment while still a child.”

So when ʿĪsā (عليه السلام) reached seven years of age, he spoke with prophethood and messengership when Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him. Thus ʿĪsā became the hujjah over Yaḥyā and over all the people. And the earth, O Abū Khālid, does not remain even for a single day without a hujjah of Allah over the people, ever since the day Allah created Ādam (عليه السلام) and settled him on the earth.”

So I said, “May I be made your ransom, was ʿAlī (عليه السلام) a hujjah from Allah and His Messenger over this Ummah during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?” He said, “Yes—on the day he established him for the people, set him up as a banner, called them to his wilayah, and commanded them to obey him.”

I said, “And was obedience to ʿAlī (عليه السلام) obligatory upon the people during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and after his passing?” He said, “Yes, but he remained silent and did not speak alongside the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). Obedience to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was binding upon his Ummah and upon ʿAlī (عليه السلام) during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). And obedience to ʿAlī (عليه السلام), from Allah and from His Messenger, was binding upon all the people after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) was wise and knowledgeable.”

key_terms.آيَةً: a sign from Allah manifesting divine power and truth
key_terms.الْحِكْمَةَ: divinely granted wisdom and sound judgment

key_terms.طَاعَتِهِ: obedience owed to him by divine command

ai.seo_question: Was Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام) Allah’s hujjah during the lifetime of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) and after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that divine proof (ḥujjah) remains continuously on the earth, illustrated through the lives of ʿĪsā, Zakariyyā, and Yaḥyā (عليهم السلام). It then applies this principle to Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام), affirming his divinely mandated authority and obligatory obedience after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).
